text:
IncidentBot: ALERT 18:00 UTC — SLO breach detected: /v1/generate p99 > 6s (SLO target 2s). Auto-threshold triggered. Severity: SEV3.

Ash Lee: noticed customer reports ~18:01 UTC about streaming stalls. Investigating. @oncall-bot who is on-call?

oncall-bot: Jamal Rivera is on-call until 14:00 UTC. Paging Jamal.

Jamal Rivera: got it, looking. I see p95 jumped ~2.1s -> 4.5s and p99 to ~6.8s in the last 7m. Streaming stalls count up ~15% of sessions.

Mike Patel: adding metrics — from prometheus: 
- generate_request_duration_seconds: p95=4.6s p99=6.8s
- streaming_stall_rate{route="/v1/generate"}=0.153
- prefix_cache_hit_rate=0.28 (usually ~0.86)
- prefix_cache_miss_rate spike at 72% for keys with prefix-hash v2

Sofia Nguyen: prefix_cache_hit_rate drop stands out. Any recent rollout that touched prefix hashing or cache key format?

Remy Cole: yep, there was a runtime change this morning that switched prefix hashing to v2 to reduce collisions — commit abcd123 (eng-runtime). Deployed at 10:23 UTC, gradual rollout to 50% nodes.

Ash Lee: could the v2 hash be incompatible with cached entries from older nodes leading to widespread cold-cache?

Remy Cole: that's my suspicion. If keys changed, backend would treat many prefixes as new, causing misses and higher backend load -> tail latency.

Jamal Rivera: quick check on shard logs shows many "cache_miss: key_prefix=<user-prefix> hash=v2 no-entry" and backend request queue depth spiked. Pushing KV requests to storage backend — increase in 503s from origin.

Mike Patel: customer impact: our telemetry flags ~3 enterprise tenants with >40% of requests hitting p99 and degraded streaming. ~2k active streams across those tenants showing stalls. Free-tier latencies also up but less customer-visible.

Ash Lee: mitigation ideas: 1) roll back prefix-hash rollout to v1, 2) enable compat-mode to accept both v1/v2 key forms, 3) route high-traffic customers to dedicated pools to isolate. Which is fastest?

Remy Cole: fastest small-blast: rollback the rollout flag to 0% so all nodes use v1. I've prepared the rollback command. If rollback is risky we can enable compat-mode in the cache layer first (reads legacy keys as fallback).

Jamal Rivera: I'll run rollback now and keep an eye on latency. Running command: 

```
kubectl -n eng-runtime set env deployment/eng-runtime ROLLOUT_PREFIX_HASH=v1 --record
# or via featureflag service
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/feature/prefix-hash/rollback -d '{"target":"v1"}'
```

Remy Cole: 👍 make sure to also flush local in-memory prefix caches on nodes that already served v2 keys (evict-only, short TTL) — otherwise they might continue producing v2 keys for a bit.

Jamal Rivera: rollback initiated at 18:08 UTC. Observing...

IncidentBot: UPDATE 18:09 UTC — rollback job started (job id: 0af2). Target: 50 -> 0%.

Mike Patel: metrics 18:12 UTC: p95 down to 3.2s, p99 4.9s, streaming stalls from 15% -> 9%. prefix_cache_hit_rate creeping up to 0.52. Partial recovery.

Sofia Nguyen: starting a targeted reroute for top-affected enterprise tenants to Dedicated pools (manual routing rule) until full recovery. Doing one tenant at a time.

Ash Lee: Jamal, after rollback completes, plan to run a compat-read deploy (reads both v1 and v2 keys) and then do a safe, all-at-once migration with a TTL footprint so caches converge. Also add a preflight check for cache-hit-rate delta during future prefix changes.

Remy Cole: Agreed. Also file for a rollback playbook in eng-runtime runbook: include steps to toggle flag, flush local caches, and a staged traffic shift plan. I'll open the PR.

Jamal Rivera: rollback job completed 18:20 UTC. Verifying cluster states and cache key versions... no further v2 writes observed in the next 2m window.

Mike Patel: 18:26 UTC metrics: p95=2.1s, p99=2.9s, streaming stalls 3.2%, prefix_cache_hit_rate=0.84. Looks like we are back within SLO for most routes.

Ash Lee: customer outreach: SRE -> support -> account teams: prepare a short postmortem note for the three affected customers, include root cause (prefix-hash change caused cold cache spike), actions taken (rollback + routing + follow-up fixes). Assign someone to own communication.

Sofia Nguyen: I'll coordinate with support and product for the customer note. Draft ETA 60m.

Jamal Rivera: oncall handoff note: I'm going to remain oncall for 30m for watchful monitoring then hand to next oncall if everything stays green.

IncidentBot: RESOLVE-CHECK at 18:40 UTC — automated check: p99 <= 3s for 10m window. Condition satisfied. Marking incident as mitigated; keeping SEV3 until postmortem.

Remy Cole: follow-ups (tracked): 1) add pre-deploy load-sim check for prefix-hash changes, 2) implement compat-mode read fallback, 3) update rollout to include cache-warm step, 4) run small chaos test to simulate key-format flips.

Ash Lee: thanks team. I'll start the postmortem doc and link the commit and rollback actions. Closing thread once postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:
